clue.text: "White Girl" Verdi composed — seeker for sunken treasure

parts.note: Pearl is a girl's name, and pearl is also a shade of white

indicators.note: composed in the sense of put together anew, so the letters of Verdi are rearranged

explanation.surface: A composer's opera about a pale heroine is linked, oddly, to someone hunting treasure on the seabed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed' tempts you towards Verdi the composer, but it is the anagram signal: VERDI rearranged gives DIVER.
explanation.definitionFit: Divers who bring up oysters from the seabed hunt for the gems inside, a prized underwater treasure.

clue.text: Key to picture-puzzle a volcano

parts.note: E is a musical key
a rebus is a puzzle in which pictures stand for words or syllables

explanation.surface: The solution to a picture puzzle turns out to be a volcano.
explanation.walkthrough: Mount Erebus is the active volcano on Ross Island in Antarctica.
explanation.definitionFit: Erebus is a proper name: the Antarctic mountain that erupts, named after a ship of Ross's expedition.

clue.text: Fragrant hand-out landlord's due to receive

indicators.note: the payment owed to the landlord takes in, or receives, the other piece inside it

parts.note: what a tenant owes the landlord is rent
the dole is a state hand-out to the unemployed

explanation.surface: A sweet-smelling benefit payment is just what the landlord is waiting to collect as rent.
explanation.definitionFit: Redolent means smelling strongly, usually pleasantly, so perfumed or scented.

clue.text: Philosopher destroyed its' decorum

indicators.note: destroyed means the words its and decorum are broken up and rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: Some thinker has ruined the dignity of a place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'destroyed' rearranges ITS plus DECORUM. Democritus was the Greek philosopher who proposed that everything is made of atoms.
explanation.definitionFit: Democritus was an ancient Greek thinker, the founder with Leucippus of atomic theory.

clue.text: Helping a fish to sort of travel, name this fin

definitions.text: Helping a fish to sort of travel, name this fin

indicators.note: sort of signals a loose version of the word travel, its letters rearranged along with the extra one

explanation.surface: A riddle asking for the fin that helps a fish get about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sort of' rearranges TRAVEL with N added. The ventral fins sit on a fish's underside and help it steer and balance as it swims.
explanation.definitionFit: Ventral means on the belly side, and the paired fins there help a fish move through water.

clue.text: Goods carrier loses head in the main body of also-rans

indicators.note: losing its head means the first letter of the vehicle word is dropped

parts.note: a truck carries goods

explanation.surface: A lorry driver, having lost his head, ends up in the middle of the also-rans.
explanation.walkthrough: In racing, the ruck is the bunched mass of runners behind the leaders, the ones with no chance.
explanation.definitionFit: The ruck is the crowd of horses or runners left behind, the undistinguished pack of losers.

clue.text: Disturb by repatriating colonists?

explanation.surface: Sending settlers home is a disturbing business.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as UN-SETTLE, the word means to undo a settlement, as when colonists are sent back home; the question mark flags that playful reading.
explanation.definitionFit: To unsettle is to upset or agitate; whimsically, undoing a settlement by removing its settlers.

clue.text: Shaw's heroine upset by applicants

annotationWithheld.why: Shaw's heroine upset by applicants: CANDIDA + TES, where TES can only come from 'upset' read as SET plus 'up' (reversed in a down clue), one word as both fodder and indicator

clue.text: Where to pick up some tropical bug, and antidote

definitions.text: Where to pick up some tropical bug, and antidote

indicators.note: some signals that only part of the run of words bug, and antidote is used, the letters running across them

explanation.surface: A traveller's warning about a tropical bug and the remedy for it.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run from the end of 'bug' through 'and' into 'antidote'. Uganda is a tropical African country where you might catch such a bug.
explanation.definitionFit: Uganda is an equatorial East African country, a place where a traveller might catch a tropical disease.

clue.text: Butch type seen round the roads, driving cattle

definitions.note: the clue phrase describes what the person does; the answer is the person doing it

indicators.note: the macho man is seen placed around the other piece, which goes inside him

parts.note: a he-man is a butch, macho type
RDS is the abbreviation for roads

explanation.surface: A macho figure is spotted out on the roads, driving his cattle along.
explanation.definitionFit: A herdsman is a drover, the person who tends and moves livestock.

clue.text: Be careful to receive Governor Edward

parts.note: to receive is to take
HE stands for His Excellency, the title of a colonial governor
Ed is short for Edward

explanation.surface: A warning to look out when admitting the governor, a man called Edward.
explanation.definitionFit: To take heed is to pay attention and watch out, a call for caution.

clue.text: Man in church, say?

indicators.note: say signals that a word is to be spoken, giving another of the same sound

parts.note: an aisle is a passage found in a church

explanation.surface: Asking whether a man in church might be a clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Man' looks like a person but is the Isle of Man, the island in the Irish Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Man is an island, so Man is an example of one.

clue.text: Without the Spanish entry, show is lacking refinement

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the word for show goes around the other piece

parts.note: to indicate is to show
el is Spanish for the, here entered into the other word

explanation.surface: A show left without its Spanish contribution is rather lacking in finesse.
explanation.definitionFit: Indelicate means coarse or tactless, wanting in good taste and polish.

clue.text: Made fresh alteration to instrument without notice, right?

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the instrument word surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: a reed is a wind instrument, or the vibrating part of one
an ad, short for advertisement, is a notice
just means right or fair

explanation.surface: Someone retuned an instrument without warning, and asks if that was right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but means outside: REED goes around AD and JUST.
explanation.definitionFit: To have readjusted something is to have changed or set it again, a renewed modification.

clue.text: Has this company some connexion with cattle?

definitions.text: Has this company some connexion with cattle?

parts.words: Has this company some connexion with cattle?
parts.note: a company owned by shareholders in common is pictured as if it were connected with livestock, since stock also means cattle and a joint is a cut of meat

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a business has something to do with livestock.
explanation.walkthrough: A joint-stock company is owned by shareholders; stock also means livestock, hence the cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: A joint-stock company has capital held jointly by shareholders, the ordinary form of a corporation.

clue.text: How office bosses lay down the law

explanation.surface: Office managers are bossy about rules.
explanation.walkthrough: Bosses once spoke letters aloud for a secretary to take down; the same verb means to give orders.
explanation.definitionFit: Bosses dictate letters to secretaries; to dictate also means to command with authority.

clue.text: Flirtatious type of bird took food, some say

indicators.note: some say signals that the words are spoken, giving something that sounds the same

parts.note: a cock is a bird and ate means took food

explanation.surface: A flirt is described as some sort of bird that ate its food.
explanation.definitionFit: A coquette is a woman who flirts, teasing admirers without serious intent.

clue.text: No end of a baby, this balladmonger

definitions.text: No end of a baby, this balladmonger

parts.words: No end of a baby, this balladmonger
parts.note: a baby cut short is Bab, the pen name under which a Victorian librettist published his comic Bab Ballads

explanation.surface: A ballad-writer who is endlessly babyish.
explanation.walkthrough: W.S. Gilbert, librettist to Sullivan, signed his illustrated comic verse 'Bab', baby with its last letter gone, hence the Bab Ballads.
explanation.definitionFit: W.S. Gilbert wrote the Bab Ballads, comic verse, so he was a writer of ballads.

clue.text: Rustic asks if this monster is one of Titania's attendants

parts.note: in rustic dialect 'is he' becomes 'be he'
Moth is one of the fairies serving Titania in A Midsummer Night's Dream

explanation.surface: A country bumpkin wonders whether this monster is one of the fairy queen's servants.
explanation.walkthrough: Titania is the fairy queen in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream; her fairies include Peaseblossom, Cobweb, Moth and Mustardseed.
explanation.definitionFit: Behemoth is the huge beast of the Book of Job, hence any enormous creature.

clue.text: It's right to pass and fall back

parts.note: time is said to pass or elapse

explanation.surface: Advice that it's fine to give up and retreat.
explanation.definitionFit: To relapse is to slip back into a former, worse state, as an illness returning.

clue.text: Various clients accept that French is in the melting-pot

indicators.note: the rearranged letters take in, or accept, the other piece inside them
various suggests the letters of clients in a different arrangement

parts.note: que is French for that

explanation.surface: Assorted customers agree that France is in a state of flux.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Various' rearranges CLIENTS into LISCENT, which takes in QUE after LI.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquescent means becoming liquid, so melting.

clue.text: Artist owns about fifty

indicators.note: about means around, so the word for owns goes around the other piece

parts.note: to own is to have, so owns means has
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A painter possesses some fifty works.
explanation.definitionFit: Frans Hals was a Dutch Golden Age painter, famous for The Laughing Cavalier.

clue.text: Pope's man, say, comes in after time

indicators.note: the abbreviation comes in, going inside the other word

parts.note: late means after the expected time
eg, for example, is what say means here

explanation.surface: The Pope's representative turns up behind schedule.
explanation.definitionFit: A legate is a papal envoy, a cleric sent to represent the Vatican.

clue.text: Water plant by the mountain loved by a Trojan prince

definitions.note: the clue phrase describes a person; the answer is that person

parts.note: cress, as in watercress, is a plant grown in water
Mount Ida is the mountain near Troy

explanation.surface: A watercress patch beside the mountain is cherished by a prince of Troy.
explanation.walkthrough: In Chaucer and Shakespeare, Troilus, son of King Priam of Troy, loves Cressida, who betrays him.
explanation.definitionFit: Cressida is the faithless lover of Troilus in the medieval Trojan legend.

clue.text: "Then fall, Caesar!"

parts.note: these are Caesar's last words in Shakespeare's play, spoken as he is stabbed on the day of March the soothsayer warned him of

explanation.walkthrough: In Julius Caesar, 'Et tu, Brute? Then fall, Caesar!' is spoken at his assassination on 15 March.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ides of March, the fifteenth day, was the date Caesar was assassinated in the Senate.

clue.text: It may lead to marriage for a river girl

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
the Po is the great river of northern Italy
Sal is a girl's name, short for Sally or Sarah

explanation.surface: Something that might end in a wedding is attributed to a girl from the riverside.
explanation.definitionFit: Asking someone to wed is the step that can result in getting married.

clue.text: Story about the race is just gossip

indicators.note: the story goes about, or around, the race abbreviation

parts.note: a tale is a story
the TT, Tourist Trophy, is the motorcycle race on the Isle of Man

explanation.surface: An account of the race that is nothing but hearsay.
explanation.walkthrough: The TT is the famous Isle of Man motorcycle race.
explanation.definitionFit: Tattle is idle chatter and telling tales, the same as gossip.

clue.text: Disconcerting if he's taken your watch for instance

definitions.text: Disconcerting if he's taken your watch for instance

indicators.note: disconcerting means throwing into disorder, so the letters of if he's taken are jumbled

explanation.surface: It would be upsetting if someone had pinched your watch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disconcerting' rearranges IF HES TAKEN; the whole clue also describes the furtive pickpocket who would take a watch.
explanation.definitionFit: A sneak thief steals stealthily, without force, such as lifting a watch unnoticed.
